searchAudit.objective: Explore Agentic Driving safety-runtime candidates at the boundary between cognitive proposals and independently enforced vehicle actions, while requiring attack-to-action penetration, recoverable fallback, verifier distribution validity, and explicit minimum-risk behavior after timeout or rejection.
searchAudit.window: Primary records available through 2026-08-01, with emphasis on 2024-2026 Agentic Driving, VLA security, runtime assurance, safety filtering, and driving-verifier work.
rulesApplied: No scores, acceptance-threshold guesses, or idea-center writes.
A language or tool anomaly counts only when it changes an executable action or the post-rejection state that generates later actions.
A verifier must be independent in authority and evaluated under planner-induced and attack-induced distribution shift.
Fallback is evaluated as a closed-loop state transition, including re-entry and minimum-risk terminal behavior, rather than as a named controller.
Generic shields, prompt-injection benchmarks, rule checkers, uncertainty gates, CBF wrappers, and Simplex transfers are collision baselines rather than novelty claims.
Repository presence, dependency repair, and synthetic fixtures are excluded from task-level evidence.
searchAudit.canonicalization: DOI, venue, OpenReview, and arXiv aliases were collapsed to one primary record. Formal venue pages were preferred when available; recent preprints retain arXiv identifiers.
limitations: No full VLA checkpoint or CARLA closed loop was executed locally, so no claim is made that cognitive-state contamination naturally occurs after a rejected driving action.

The executed CommonRoad path checks sampled oriented-rectangle overlap at the official 0.1 second trajectory points; it is not a swept-volume, road-boundary, dynamics, or formal reachability certificate.
The CommonRoad native drivability-checker build remained blocked and is explicitly excluded from evidence; no further persistent dependency work was performed.
Several 2026 records are preprints or withdrawn OpenReview submissions and are used only for functional collision, not maturity claims.

sourceAttempts.note: Local reviews and reports supplied scoped leads and limitation statements; every included reference uses an official primary destination rather than counting the local synthesis as a source.
Used for current technical reports and original method papers without a preferred formal destination.
CVF, ACL Anthology, AAAI, USENIX, IEEE, ICML, and official institutional publication pages were used for formal records.
Used for current ICLR, workshop, and robotics safety records with publication status kept explicit.
Three official repositories were fixed to commits. CommonRoad supplied a real scenario and trajectory consequence path; VLM-CASE supplied scenarios but no released implementation.

functionalCollisionAudit.occupiedFunction: Pre-execution rejection, independent authority, fallback switching, reverse switching, and monitor-controller cooperation are already explicit mechanisms.
functionalCollisionAudit.residualRequired: A surviving idea must identify a driving-specific state or estimand outside plant/action authority and prove that it changes later executable actions.

functionalCollisionAudit.occupiedFunction: Minimally invasive projection into a safe control set and distribution-aware policy filtering are established.
functionalCollisionAudit.residualRequired: A VLA wrapper is insufficient unless it exposes a new failure caused by cognitive state or verifier mismatch that ordinary filtering cannot handle.

functionalCollisionAudit.occupiedFunction: Text, visual, physical, backdoor, freezing, and language-channel attack surfaces already have benchmark formulations.
functionalCollisionAudit.residualRequired: The attack must cross an independent action boundary or persist after rejection; attack success on text or model output alone is not enough.

functionalCollisionAudit.occupiedFunction: Candidate scoring, geometric refinement, reachability checks, path-consistent filtering, and context-conditioned envelopes already validate or repair actions.
functionalCollisionAudit.residualRequired: A contribution must test verifier validity on planner-induced or attack-induced support, rather than adding another learned score or rule checker.

functionalCollisionAudit.occupiedFunction: Immediate fallback, delayed fallback, recovery deadlines, and handback are already studied.
functionalCollisionAudit.residualRequired: A surviving result must show that the cognitive subsystem makes a nominally safe handback unsafe and that a distinct protocol fixes it.

verifiedReferences.title: ReasonBreak: Probing Vulnerabilities in Reasoning-Enabled Vision-Language-Action Models for Autonomous Driving
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Perturbs the reasoning text channel in open-loop and sampled closed-loop evaluation; it shows behavioral propagation but does not identify natural occurrence or a reasoning mediator.

verifiedReferences.title: VLADriveBench: Evaluating CoT-Action Relationship in VLA for Autonomous Driving
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Uses mid-pass CoT interventions and selfsplice controls to distinguish observational alignment from causal action influence.

verifiedReferences.title: VLM-CASE: Vision-Language Model Enabled Context-Adaptive Safety Envelopes for Anticipatory Safe Autonomous Driving
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Maps semantic context into physical and RSS-style safety-envelope parameters while keeping a conventional planner/controller interface.

verifiedReferences.title: DriveVer: Lightweight Trajectory Evaluator as Test-Time Verifier for Autonomous Driving
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Trains a compact dual-head verifier on NAVSIM candidate trajectories to score and geometrically refine plans.

verifiedReferences.title: Mission-Level Runtime Assurance Framework for Autonomous Driving
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Rejects unsafe or mission-infeasible high-level commands before execution and switches to fallback; remaining failures include cases where fallback activates but cannot recover.

verifiedReferences.title: Simplex-Drive: An AI-Based Runtime Assurance Framework for Autonomous Vehicles
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Applies a Simplex-style decision module and safety controller to autonomous driving.

verifiedReferences.title: Black-Box Simplex Architecture for Runtime Assurance of Autonomous CPS
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Provides runtime assurance around a black-box advanced controller through monitor-triggered control transfer.

verifiedReferences.title: Neural Simplex Architecture
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Adds reverse switching and online correction of an advanced neural controller after failover.

verifiedReferences.title: Synergistic Simplex: Cooperative Runtime Assurance for Safety-Critical Autonomous Systems
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Allows bounded bidirectional use of ML outputs by safety monitors while preserving formal safety conditions.

verifiedReferences.title: Conformal Recovery-Deadline Certificates for Runtime Assurance of Adapting Controllers
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Uses split-conformal recovery-time bounds to permit delayed fallback while retaining a verified hard-limit monitor.

verifiedReferences.title: In-Distribution Barrier Functions: Self-Supervised Policy Filters that Avoid Out-of-Distribution States
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Wraps a visual policy with a learned latent-state barrier intended to stay near safe-demonstration support.

verifiedReferences.title: Safety Evaluation of Motion Plans Using Trajectory Predictors as Forward Reachable Set Estimators
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Builds conformally calibrated forward reachable sets from trajectory predictors to check ego motion plans.

verifiedReferences.title: From Demonstrations to Safe Deployment: Path-Consistent Safety Filtering for Diffusion Policies
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Uses path-consistent braking and set-based reachability so a filter preserves demonstrated action-sequence structure.

verifiedReferences.title: Can Control Barrier Functions Keep Automated Vehicles Safe in Live Freeway Traffic?
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Evaluates a CBF-supervised automated vehicle in live congested freeway car following, including invariance and recovery properties.

verifiedReferences.title: Physical Backdoor Attack Can Jeopardize Driving with Vision-Large-Language Models
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Demonstrates a physical visual backdoor against driving VLM responses; it does not execute a full independent vehicle-control stack.

verifiedReferences.title: Visual Adversarial Attack on Vision-Language Models for Autonomous Driving
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Studies visual adversarial manipulation of autonomous-driving VLMs and reports digital and small-platform evidence.

verifiedReferences.title: Black-Box Adversarial Attack on Vision Language Models for Autonomous Driving
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Defines black-box attacks against driving VLM outputs, occupying a generic adversarial benchmark formulation.

verifiedReferences.title: SafeCoop: Unravelling Full Stack Safety in Agentic Cooperative Driving
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Combines semantic firewalling, language-perception consistency, and multi-source consensus under closed-loop CARLA attacks.

verifiedReferences.title: FreezeVLA: Action-Freezing Attacks against Vision-Language-Action Models
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Optimizes adversarial images that induce cross-prompt action freezing across robot VLA models.

verifiedReferences.title: Plug in the Safety Chip: Enforcing Constraints for LLM-driven Robot Agents
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Translates natural-language prohibitions into LTL constraints, prunes unsafe actions, and requests replanning.

verifiedReferences.title: Bench2Drive-Robust: Benchmarking Closed-Loop Autonomous Driving under Deployment Perturbations
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Injects camera-stream faults, ego-state errors, and inference delays in closed-loop driving, providing a non-adversarial runtime-fault baseline.

verifiedReferences.title: Validate the Dream Before You Trust Its Verdict: Admissibility for World-Model Simulators
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Treats simulator or world-model admissibility as a prerequisite for accepting a downstream safety verdict.

verifiedReferences.title: A Stitch in Time Saves Nine: Preserving Policy Compatibility Under Perception Updates in End-to-End Autonomous Driving
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Shows that upstream perception changes can break a frozen downstream policy and proposes compatibility-preserving adaptation.

verifiedReferences.title: Shift & Drift: A Zero-Shot Benchmark for Generalizable and Robust Autonomous Driving Motion Planning
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Evaluates planning under distribution shift and drift, relevant to planner-verifier support mismatch.

verifiedReferences.title: Cognitive Dual-Process Planning for Autonomous Driving with Structured Scene Knowledge and Verifiable Reasoning-Action Consistency
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Routes between fast and structured slow planning and checks rule consistency, but does not certify continuous vehicle trajectories or post-rejection state recovery.

verifiedReferences.title: AgentThink: A Unified Framework for Tool-Augmented Chain-of-Thought Reasoning in Vision-Language Models for Autonomous Driving
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Trains tool-augmented driving reasoning and evaluates tool invocation; downstream action mediation is not independently isolated.

verifiedReferences.title: LMDrive: Closed-Loop End-to-End Driving with Large Language Models
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Provides a language-conditioned CARLA closed-loop baseline and natural-language instruction failure surface.

verifiedReferences.title: SimLingo: Vision-Only Closed-Loop Autonomous Driving with Language-Action Alignment
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Provides a closed-loop language-action aligned driving policy and public benchmark path.

verifiedReferences.title: OpenDriveVLA: Towards End-to-end Autonomous Driving with Large Vision Language Action Model
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Provides an open VLA action model and documented trajectory-evaluation path, subject to substantial data and dependency setup.

verifiedReferences.title: ORION: A Holistic End-to-End Autonomous Driving Framework by Vision-Language Instructed Action Generation
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Connects long-term context, language reasoning, and a generative planner; VLADriveBench finds its visible CoT can be weakly causal.

verifiedReferences.title: Counterfactual VLA: Self-Reflective Vision-Language-Action Model with Adaptive Reasoning
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Selectively invokes counterfactual reasoning and revises meta-actions, occupying generic same-model repair and adaptive-reasoning claims.

verifiedReferences.title: C-CoT: Counterfactual Chain-of-Thought with Vision-Language Models for Safe Autonomous Driving
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Uses a structured counterfactual action tree for critical objects, risk, alternatives, and final planning.

verifiedReferences.title: Guardauto: A Decentralized Runtime Protection System for Autonomous Driving
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Isolates autonomous-driving components and coordinates local runtime protection to diagnose cascading failures.

verifiedReferences.title: Robust Physical-World Attacks on Deep Learning Visual Classification
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Establishes realizable printed physical perturbations against traffic-sign classification, but not full-stack driving action effects.

verifiedReferences.title: Dirty Road Can Attack: Security of Deep Learning Based Automated Lane Centering under Physical-World Attack
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Connects a realizable road patch to lane-centering behavior and simulation-level driving consequences.

verifiedReferences.title: Invisible for Both Camera and LiDAR: Security of Multi-Sensor Fusion Based Perception in Autonomous Driving under Physical-World Attacks
verifiedReferences.venue: IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy 2021
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Attacks camera-LiDAR fusion through physical-world manipulations and separates sensor, platform, and simulated collision evidence.

verifiedReferences.title: You Can't See Me: Physical Removal Attacks on LiDAR-Based Autonomous Vehicles Driving Frameworks
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Demonstrates physical removal attacks against LiDAR-based driving frameworks with explicit platform and simulation evidence boundaries.

verifiedReferences.title: A First Physical-World Trajectory Prediction Attack via LiDAR-Induced Deceptions in Autonomous Driving
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Pushes physical LiDAR deception into trajectory prediction and planning output, supplying a direct attack-to-action comparator.

verifiedReferences.title: Empowering Autonomous Driving with Large Language Models: A Safety Perspective
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Pairs LLM behavior planning with MPC and a safety-verifier shield in simulation, directly occupying generic LLM-plus-shield designs.

verifiedReferences.title: Safety Filters: A Unified View from Robust Control to Reinforcement Learning
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Systematizes safety-filter structures, intervention objectives, and assumptions; used as a functional-equivalence map rather than a novelty source.

verifiedReferences.title: Run Time Assurance for Safety-Critical Systems: An Introduction to Safety Filtering Approaches for Complex Control Systems
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Defines the established RTA design space of monitors, backup controllers, switching, and safety filtering.

candidateLedger.title: Transactional cognitive-state commit only after independent action acceptance
candidateLedger.hypothesis: A proposal rejected by an independent trajectory verifier may still mutate conversation memory, recurrent state, tool cache, or planner belief and thereby cause unsafe later actions; committing cognitive state only after action acceptance could remove that persistence.
candidateLedger.naturalEvidence: ReasonBreak demonstrates text-to-behavior propagation, but neither it nor the inspected public assets demonstrate that a rejected action leaves a harmful cognitive state that later survives clean input.
candidateLedger.nearestWorkComparison: Neural Simplex already handles handback and advanced-controller correction; Guardauto handles component isolation; the local memory-tool pool already rejected tool-result withdrawal debt for missing occurrence and public closed-loop evidence.
officialAssets: a future pinned stateful VLA checkpoint
candidateLedger.minimumEntry: Show at least one naturally arising or source-faithful ReasonBreak perturbation where action t is rejected, clean observations resume, and the same fixed model emits a harmful action at t+1 or later solely because rejected-branch state persisted.
candidateLedger.twoWeekBudget: Days 1-2 pin a stateful public VLA and checkpoint or stop. Days 3-5 log pre/post hidden, textual, and tool state around verifier rejection. Days 6-9 compare commit, rollback, full reset, and latching fallback. Days 10-14 replay paired routes and audit every claimed persistence event.
candidateLedger.successCondition: Rejected-branch state causes repeatable later executable harm under clean resumed input, while transactional commit removes it without the progress loss of full reset or latching fallback.
candidateLedger.killCondition: No post-rejection persistence occurs, only injected synthetic memory creates it, full reset or ordinary Simplex matches the result, or no public stateful VLA path closes by day 2.
candidateLedger.positiveResultValue: Would identify a safety boundary that action-only runtime assurance does not govern: commit ordering for cognition that survives a veto.
candidateLedger.negativeResultValue: Would rule out a speculative recovery hazard and support simpler action-only shielding plus ordinary handback.

candidateLedger.title: Compile cognitive advice into a separate physical safety envelope
candidateLedger.hypothesis: Semantic scene advice can modify friction, headway, visibility, or RSS parameters while a conventional controller remains authoritative.
candidateLedger.naturalEvidence: VLM-CASE directly implements this semantic-to-envelope pattern.
candidateLedger.nearestWorkComparison: VLM-CASE is functionally direct; the LLM safety-perspective work also pairs language behavior planning with MPC and a verifier shield.
candidateLedger.minimumEntry: Identify a distinct contract not reducible to context-conditioned envelope parameters and show an action consequence unavailable to VLM-CASE.
candidateLedger.twoWeekBudget: Reimplement three public VLM-CASE scenarios with a conventional envelope and compare any proposed semantic contract under identical classifier errors and stale-context faults.
candidateLedger.successCondition: A new contract handles an identified failure that the direct baselines cannot express while retaining independent action authority.
candidateLedger.killCondition: The method is equivalent to changing envelope parameters, adding rules, or gating on semantic confidence.
candidateLedger.positiveResultValue: Would clarify which cognitive outputs can safely influence a control envelope.
candidateLedger.negativeResultValue: Would consolidate the problem under VLM-CASE-style context adaptation rather than create a duplicate direction.

candidateLedger.title: Reject driving tool outputs that lack typed capability and freshness contracts
candidateLedger.hypothesis: Tool results should reach the planner only when schema, provenance, scope, freshness, and action capability checks pass.
candidateLedger.naturalEvidence: AgentThink exposes tool use, but the inspected evidence does not show a tool-contract failure causing an executable driving action.
candidateLedger.nearestWorkComparison: Safety Chip already compiles language constraints and prunes unsafe actions; SafeCoop performs semantic firewall and consistency checks; generic typed-tool validation is established software assurance.
candidateLedger.minimumEntry: Show a naturally occurring driving tool output that passes ordinary schema/provenance checks yet violates an action-specific capability contract and produces route-level harm.
candidateLedger.twoWeekBudget: Pin one AgentThink task path, enumerate tool-result contracts, replay natural failures, and compare schema, provenance, freshness, and action-specific contract ablations.
candidateLedger.successCondition: An action-specific contract prevents natural route-level harm missed by all generic validation baselines.
candidateLedger.killCondition: Only malformed or injected outputs fail, or schema/provenance/freshness checks are sufficient.
candidateLedger.positiveResultValue: Would define a concrete rejection boundary for driving tools.
candidateLedger.negativeResultValue: Would show that ordinary tool assurance is adequate and avoid a driving-specific rename.

candidateLedger.title: Measure whether ReasonBreak corruption crosses an independent action verifier
candidateLedger.hypothesis: Reasoning corruption is operationally important only when its trajectory leaves the independently accepted action set or changes later closed-loop state.
candidateLedger.naturalEvidence: ReasonBreak reports trajectory and closed-loop impact; VLADriveBench already supplies causal CoT interventions and selfsplice controls.
candidateLedger.nearestWorkComparison: Combining these attacks with a verifier adds an evaluation stage but does not create a new mechanism; the local reasoning-action pool already retains safety-bounded reasoning influence.
candidateLedger.minimumEntry: Discover a penetration mechanism that changes verifier semantics or post-rejection recovery, rather than reporting another attack success rate.
candidateLedger.twoWeekBudget: Replay fixed text interventions, convert trajectories to the CommonRoad checker interface, and report verifier pass, reject, fallback, and route consequence with selfsplice controls.
candidateLedger.successCondition: A reproducible attack class crosses an independent verifier or corrupts recovery through a mechanism absent from the source benchmarks.
candidateLedger.killCondition: All effects are blocked by ordinary action checking or reduce to existing CoT-action intervention results.
candidateLedger.positiveResultValue: Would locate the exact boundary where reasoning attacks become executable hazards.
candidateLedger.negativeResultValue: Would show that existing independent action validation contains the tested reasoning attacks.

candidateLedger.title: Benchmark persistent cognitive contamination after an action veto
candidateLedger.hypothesis: A vetoed proposal can remain in memory and alter later plans even after the attacking input disappears.
candidateLedger.naturalEvidence: No inspected driving source demonstrates this event; generic agent-memory poisoning only establishes an analogous software risk.
candidateLedger.nearestWorkComparison: This is the diagnostic half of transactional state commit and collides with generic persistent-memory attack benchmarking.
candidateLedger.minimumEntry: Observe source-faithful post-veto persistence without manually writing the malicious content into memory.
candidateLedger.twoWeekBudget: Instrument a public stateful planner, pair rollback and non-rollback episodes, and aggregate later action violations by route rather than token or frame.
candidateLedger.successCondition: Natural or source-faithful veto events produce delayed action harm attributable to retained state.
candidateLedger.killCondition: Persistence appears only after artificial memory insertion, does not change actions, or cannot be reproduced on a public model.
candidateLedger.positiveResultValue: Would establish the missing occurrence evidence for transactional cognitive-state safety.
candidateLedger.negativeResultValue: Would close a speculative attack branch and prevent a benchmark-only publication.

candidateLedger.title: Cross-support contract between an updated planner and learned action verifier
candidateLedger.hypothesis: A verifier trained on one planner's candidates may falsely accept or reject trajectories from a new planner, an attacked planner, or a safety-filter repair distribution.
candidateLedger.naturalEvidence: DriveVer is trained on a constructed NAVSIM candidate distribution; Policy Stitching and Shift & Drift establish component and planning distribution shifts, but no inspected result isolates verifier failure after planner replacement.
candidateLedger.nearestWorkComparison: PACS explicitly preserves policy path consistency, IDBF filters distribution shift, and FRS work calibrates coverage. A generic cross-fit or uncertainty gate is already occupied.
candidateLedger.minimumEntry: Show a planner replacement that reverses verifier error at matched physical risk and cannot be fixed by held-out cross-planner calibration.
candidateLedger.twoWeekBudget: Generate candidates from two public planners or archived candidate sets, train on one, test on the other and on safety-filter repairs, then compare conformal, OOD, and rule-based monitors.
candidateLedger.successCondition: A stable, action-relevant mismatch remains after strong calibration and motivates a distinct planner-verifier contract.
candidateLedger.killCondition: Cross-validation, conformal recalibration, or a deterministic checker removes the effect, or no two public planner outputs are available.
candidateLedger.positiveResultValue: Would expose a deployment assumption hidden by same-distribution verifier metrics.
candidateLedger.negativeResultValue: Would establish that ordinary cross-planner validation is sufficient for the tested verifier.

candidateLedger.title: Switch to fallback when semantic and physical verifiers disagree
candidateLedger.hypothesis: A semantic verifier and a physical reachability checker could catch complementary unsafe actions, with disagreement triggering fallback.
candidateLedger.naturalEvidence: The sources establish complementary semantic and geometric checks but no unique disagreement mechanism.
candidateLedger.nearestWorkComparison: Safety Shell, Simplex/RTA, SafeCoop consensus, VLM-CASE, and FRS checking already cover redundant monitors plus fallback.
candidateLedger.minimumEntry: Define an identified disagreement class with task consequence and show why ordinary monitor union or conservative veto is inadequate.
candidateLedger.twoWeekBudget: Run matched candidate trajectories through semantic rules and geometry checks, classify disagreements, and compare union, intersection, learned arbitration, and immediate fallback.
candidateLedger.successCondition: A distinct arbitration rule improves route progress at matched verified safety on natural disagreements.
candidateLedger.killCondition: Conservative union or physical-only checking dominates, or disagreements are label noise.
candidateLedger.positiveResultValue: Would define when heterogeneous verifiers add value.
candidateLedger.negativeResultValue: Would favor the simpler independent physical monitor.

candidateLedger.title: Expire stale VLA actions at the control deadline and execute a leased minimum-risk action
candidateLedger.hypothesis: Every cognitive proposal should carry a short execution lease; timeout, refusal, or stale completion transfers authority to a precomputed minimum-risk action.
candidateLedger.naturalEvidence: Bench2Drive-Robust shows inference-delay harm, but does not make an action lease novel.
candidateLedger.nearestWorkComparison: RTA, contingency planning, deadline-censored value-of-thought in the local reasoning-action pool, and standard stale-command watchdogs already occupy this function.
candidateLedger.minimumEntry: Find a lease-specific failure not covered by a control deadline, watchdog, or ready fallback action.
candidateLedger.twoWeekBudget: Replay measured latency traces, compare stale execution, immediate fallback, precomputed contingency, and lease expiry at identical deadlines.
candidateLedger.successCondition: Lease semantics prevent a distinct stale-action race while preserving progress over ordinary deadline fallback.
candidateLedger.killCondition: A standard watchdog or ready fallback is functionally identical.
candidateLedger.positiveResultValue: Would clarify authority at the exact timeout boundary.
candidateLedger.negativeResultValue: Would keep timeout handling in established RTA and real-time control practice.

candidateLedger.title: Require a clean-state shadow horizon before handing control back to the cognitive planner
candidateLedger.hypothesis: After a veto, a clean shadow planner should produce verifiable actions for a horizon before regaining authority.
candidateLedger.naturalEvidence: No inspected driving VLA source demonstrates that cognitive contamination makes ordinary handback unsafe.
candidateLedger.nearestWorkComparison: Neural Simplex reverse switching and controller correction, plus conformal recovery deadlines, already cover readmission conditions and delayed handback.
candidateLedger.minimumEntry: Show that the same plant-state recovery condition is safe for a clean planner but unsafe for a contaminated planner.
candidateLedger.twoWeekBudget: Compare immediate handback, fixed clean horizon, verified shadow horizon, full reset, and latching fallback on paired stateful routes.
candidateLedger.successCondition: Cognitive-state-aware readmission prevents repeat failures missed by plant-state handback and beats full reset on progress.
candidateLedger.killCondition: Plant-state conditions suffice or no contamination event is observed.
candidateLedger.positiveResultValue: Would extend handback contracts to a demonstrated cognitive state variable.
candidateLedger.negativeResultValue: Would confirm existing reverse-switching conditions are enough.

candidateLedger.title: Choose fallback by recoverability rather than immediate collision avoidance
candidateLedger.hypothesis: Among immediately safe fallback actions, select one that preserves a future recoverable set and mission feasibility.
candidateLedger.naturalEvidence: Mission-Level RTA reports cases where fallback activates yet recovery remains insufficient, establishing the problem.
candidateLedger.nearestWorkComparison: Mission-Level RTA directly evaluates mission feasibility; reachability, viability, and contingency planning already select actions by future recoverability.
candidateLedger.minimumEntry: Identify a driving-specific recoverability state not expressible by existing mission feasibility or reachable-set contingency planning.
candidateLedger.twoWeekBudget: Enumerate safe fallback trajectories in highway-env/CommonRoad, compare immediate braking, lane-follow, reachable-set, and mission-feasible selection under identical rejected commands.
candidateLedger.successCondition: A new recoverability criterion prevents failures missed by mission-level and reachable-set baselines.
candidateLedger.killCondition: Mission feasibility or reachable-set selection already captures the gain.
candidateLedger.positiveResultValue: Would improve fallback choice in dense traffic.
candidateLedger.negativeResultValue: Would route the problem to established mission-level RTA rather than a new Agentic Driving idea.

candidateLedger.title: Map language refusal, malformed output, and silence to explicit minimum-risk states
candidateLedger.hypothesis: Different cognitive failures should deterministically select stop, lane-hold, pull-over, or contingency trajectories rather than a null action.
candidateLedger.naturalEvidence: The safety need is clear, but no new mechanism separates it from established fault-to-fallback mapping.
candidateLedger.nearestWorkComparison: Mission-Level RTA, Simplex fallback, contingency planning, and automotive minimum-risk maneuver state machines cover the functional behavior.
candidateLedger.minimumEntry: Show that language-failure semantics carry verified physical information that changes the optimal minimum-risk state beyond observable plant and route state.
candidateLedger.twoWeekBudget: Inject refusal, malformed, timeout, and contradictory outputs while holding plant state fixed; compare one fallback, fault-specific fallback, and oracle contingency selection.
candidateLedger.successCondition: Fault-specific mapping improves verified route outcomes because the failure class carries causal state information.
candidateLedger.killCondition: Observable vehicle and route state fully determine the fallback, making language class irrelevant.
candidateLedger.positiveResultValue: Would justify a typed cognitive-failure interface to MRM selection.
candidateLedger.negativeResultValue: Would simplify the interface to one generic rejection signal.

candidateLedger.title: Require every cognitive driving proposal to carry machine-checkable assumptions
candidateLedger.hypothesis: A VLA proposal should include object, rule, friction, and time-horizon assumptions that an independent checker validates before action execution.
candidateLedger.naturalEvidence: VLM-CASE already exposes semantic-to-physical assumptions, while Safety Chip checks formal constraints.
candidateLedger.nearestWorkComparison: This combines proof-carrying action, rule checking, and context-adaptive envelopes without a distinct new obligation.
candidateLedger.minimumEntry: Define an assumption whose falsification changes action safety and is neither a rule check nor an envelope parameter.
candidateLedger.twoWeekBudget: Encode assumptions for three public scenarios, compare free-text rationale, typed assumptions, direct perception checks, and oracle assumptions.
candidateLedger.successCondition: Typed assumptions detect natural unsafe proposals missed by direct physical checks and preserve useful cognitive advice.
candidateLedger.killCondition: The checker can infer the same facts directly or the proposal simply restates existing constraints.
candidateLedger.positiveResultValue: Would create an auditable boundary for cognitive influence.
candidateLedger.negativeResultValue: Would favor direct independent sensing and checking over self-reported assumptions.

candidateLedger.title: Project VLA actions through a control barrier function
candidateLedger.hypothesis: A CBF can minimally modify unsafe VLA controls while retaining task progress.
candidateLedger.naturalEvidence: CBF-supervised automated vehicles and learned in-distribution barrier filters already establish this wrapper pattern.
candidateLedger.nearestWorkComparison: This is the prohibited generic runtime-shield transfer, with no VLA-specific mechanism.
candidateLedger.minimumEntry: Demonstrate a VLA-specific state or action representation that changes the barrier problem itself.
candidateLedger.twoWeekBudget: Map candidate controls to a vehicle model and compare CBF, MPC, emergency braking, and Simplex on the same trajectories.
candidateLedger.successCondition: A new VLA-specific barrier construction is necessary and outperforms established filters under matched assumptions.
candidateLedger.killCondition: An off-the-shelf CBF or MPC filter is functionally identical.
candidateLedger.positiveResultValue: Would justify a representation-specific control contribution.
candidateLedger.negativeResultValue: Would keep VLA safety under established control filtering.

candidateLedger.title: Unified prompt and visual attack suite for driving VLAs
candidateLedger.hypothesis: A common suite could compare text corruption, physical patches, backdoors, freezing, and cooperative-language spoofing on driving actions.
candidateLedger.naturalEvidence: ReasonBreak, BadVLMDriver, ADvLM, black-box attacks, FreezeVLA, and SafeCoop already span these channels.
candidateLedger.nearestWorkComparison: The proposal aggregates and renames existing attack benchmarks without a new attack mechanism or causal estimand.
candidateLedger.minimumEntry: Produce a new realizable attack path that crosses an independent action boundary and survives adaptive defense.
candidateLedger.twoWeekBudget: Standardize threat models and replay existing attacks with action and fallback outcomes; stop if the result is only a leaderboard.
candidateLedger.successCondition: A new cross-channel mechanism creates vehicle-level harm missed by every source benchmark.
candidateLedger.killCondition: The output is a renamed benchmark or reports model-output attack success without independent action consequences.
candidateLedger.positiveResultValue: Would matter only if it reveals a new penetration mechanism.
candidateLedger.negativeResultValue: Would prevent duplicate benchmark work and preserve threat-model clarity.

candidateLedger.title: Reject actions when the language rationale and trajectory disagree
candidateLedger.hypothesis: A rationale-action consistency model can reject hallucinated or contradictory plans.
candidateLedger.naturalEvidence: VLADriveBench shows that observational consistency can coexist with epiphenomenal CoT, undermining this premise.
candidateLedger.nearestWorkComparison: Cognitive Dual-Process checks reasoning-action consistency, SafeCoop uses language-perception consistency, and DriveVer validates trajectories directly.
candidateLedger.minimumEntry: Show consistency has causal predictive value beyond direct trajectory and scene checking under selfsplice controls.
candidateLedger.twoWeekBudget: Fit a consistency verifier, run selfsplice and rationale-preserving action swaps, and compare against direct geometric and learned trajectory verifiers.
candidateLedger.successCondition: Consistency catches natural unsafe actions missed by direct verifiers and survives causal controls.
candidateLedger.killCondition: Selfsplice breaks the signal, direct action checks dominate, or the rationale is epiphenomenal.
candidateLedger.positiveResultValue: Would establish when language is valid safety evidence.
candidateLedger.negativeResultValue: Would demonstrate that rationale consistency should not control vehicle authority.

candidateLedger.title: Gate world-model safety verdicts before they influence action acceptance
candidateLedger.hypothesis: A learned simulator should issue a safety verdict only when its rollout is admissible for the current scene and candidate action.
candidateLedger.naturalEvidence: The local world-model admissibility paper directly formulates this requirement.
candidateLedger.nearestWorkComparison: Admissibility-before-verdict is already the source paper's central mechanism; applying it to VLA candidates is a method transfer.
candidateLedger.minimumEntry: Find a cognitive-state-specific admissibility failure not covered by simulator support, calibration, or model-error checks.
candidateLedger.twoWeekBudget: Compare world-model verdicts with deterministic scenario checks across in-support, shifted, and attacked candidate trajectories.
candidateLedger.successCondition: A distinct cognitive-action admissibility condition predicts harmful false-safe verdicts beyond source methods.
candidateLedger.killCondition: Existing admissibility or uncertainty checks fully explain the effect.
candidateLedger.positiveResultValue: Would constrain when learned rollouts may affect runtime authority.
candidateLedger.negativeResultValue: Would keep the contribution under existing simulator-admissibility work.

reasons: No inspected public driving path demonstrates harmful state persistence after an independent action veto.
The nearest local memory-tool candidate was already rejected on occurrence and public closed-loop gates.
VLM-CASE directly maps semantic context into physical safety envelopes.
Generic typed validation, Safety Chip constraint pruning, and SafeCoop semantic firewalling already cover the function; no natural driving action failure was shown.
ReasonBreak plus VLADriveBench plus an ordinary action verifier is an evaluation composition, not a new mechanism.
Persistent state contamination is injectible but not observed in the inspected driving assets, and a benchmark transfer alone is insufficient.
PACS, IDBF, conformal calibration, and standard cross-planner validation occupy the generic mismatch treatment; no residual mechanism was demonstrated.
Redundant monitors, conservative veto, and Simplex/Safety-Shell fallback already provide the same runtime function.
Watchdogs, RTA, contingency planning, and the existing deadline-censored reasoning candidate are functionally equivalent.
Neural Simplex and recovery-deadline work already cover readmission; cognitive-state necessity lacks occurrence evidence.
Mission-Level RTA and reachable-set contingency planning directly select for future recoverability and mission feasibility.
The physical fallback is determined by vehicle, route, and environment state unless language-failure class adds causal information, which was not shown.
Safety Chip and VLM-CASE already cover machine-checkable constraints and semantic-to-physical assumptions.
This is a generic runtime-shield transfer with direct CBF, MPC, and Simplex equivalents.
It renames or aggregates existing VLA jailbreak, visual, backdoor, freezing, and physical attack benchmarks.
VLADriveBench shows consistency need not be causal; direct trajectory validation and existing consistency checkers are stronger baselines.
The local world-model admissibility work directly occupies admissibility-before-verdict; VLA application is a method transfer.

conclusion.summary: No candidate survives both functional-equivalence and evidence gates. Runtime rejection, CBF projection, Simplex switching, semantic envelopes, attack suites, trajectory verification, timeout fallback, recoverability, and readmission all have direct prior mechanisms. The only potentially distinct residual is transactional cognitive-state commit after an action veto, but current evidence establishes injectability rather than natural post-veto persistence or later executable harm.
conclusion.highestValueUnresolvedQuestion: Does a source-faithful ReasonBreak or tool failure mutate a stateful driving planner so that, after the unsafe proposal is independently rejected and clean observations resume, a later action remains unsafe because of retained cognitive state?
conclusion.promotionRequirement: Do not shortlist transactional cognitive-state safety until a pinned public stateful VLA reproduces that delayed task consequence and ordinary full reset, action-only Simplex, Neural Simplex handback, and latching fallback are all compared on paired route episodes.

executionEvidence.passedPath: Official CommonRoad USA_US101-3_3_T-1 scenario plus official candidate trajectories produced 909 sampled-safe and 91 sampled-colliding actions; trajectory 367 was accepted and trajectory 487 was rejected at 2.9 seconds against obstacle 405.
executionEvidence.blockedReason: Native drivability-checker compilation did not close in the available environment and is excluded from evidence; no dependency repair is pursued.

conclusion.decisionRule: A candidate must add a new driving-specific mechanism or estimand beyond existing RTA, CBF, Simplex, VLA attack, and verifier functions; expose a public two-week path; bind success and failure to route/action consequences; and retain value under both positive and negative results.
